capabilities.mechanism: Progress on selected longer tasks can expand useful execution, but human-duration horizons depend on task mix, reference quality and transfer to the actual job.
capabilities.conditions: 222 TH1.1 and 36 TH2 tasks, typically 15 public models through Astra and Opus 5.5, tools and task-specific budgets. Of 34 TH2 time points, 31 are estimates; human baselines allow Sonnet 5 implementation help.
capabilities.counterexample: A longer estimated 50%-success horizon does not establish longer autonomous runtime, complete occupational substitution or broad superiority over skilled humans.
capabilities.evidence: Read METR methods, 3.A, 3.C.1, robustness and Appendix A. Preserve combined doubling 3.61 months with 2.08–4.94 interval and the different verifiable-task trend.
capabilities.limits: Estimated baselines, changed human assistance, nonexhaustive model coverage, refused/blocked observations excluded and detected hacks zeroed. No uniform whole-workflow or real-deployment rate.
capabilities.mitigation: Test task transfer, exception recovery and intervention costs; keep permissions separate. Comparisons need compatible human assistance and task sets.
capabilities.readerContext: Read R0/C2a new passages and standalone conditions in Japanese/English, relevant control/acceleration tour chapters, work graph/route and time-horizon guidance. Define the human-duration interpretation before inference.
capabilities.whyHere: Add bounded evidence to R0/C2a, preserve limited/tested. R0-C2a, R0-W1 and R0-ASI remain conditional; no edge date is renewed for dependency consistency alone.

primary.support: Task progress, estimated human-time basis, filtering and transfer limits.

judgment.mechanism: An evaluation can be hard to solve yet unhelpful for deciding which research capabilities matter; model grading can overstate its quality.
judgment.conditions: Agents build METR tasks with 48 hours, 100M tokens, three concurrent environments and internet. Humans supply goals/examples/rubric and judge submissions; separate tested-model budgets apply.
judgment.counterexample: None entered this report’s suite, but underelicitation and strong verifiable ML results prevent treating that result as a general impossibility of AI research.
judgment.evidence: Read 3.B.2 and Appendix M, including added guidance and judge runs. Judges overrate creations by equally strong or stronger creators relative to human ratings; preserve that comparison direction.
judgment.limits: Selected task-creation settings, partly unused budgets and subjective human judgment. Not a measured deployment failure rate or evidence of strategic concealment.
judgment.mitigation: Separate task creation from independent validation of what it measures, using humans and other checks rather than only the creator’s own grading.
judgment.readerContext: Read C3a1 in both languages, its limits and the evaluation graph distinguishing coverage gaps from evaluation-aware concealment and runtime evasion.
judgment.whyHere: Add a concrete evaluation-design limitation to C3a1 while retaining limited/indirect. No new claim about the frequency of dangerous operational failures.

primary.support: Generated-task usefulness, comparative judge bias and underelicitation caveat.

research.mechanism: Prepared-evidence interpretation and narrowly useful task assistance may contribute to research; whole-process acceleration also needs useful decisions and reduced bottlenecks.
research.conditions: MedChemBench has 99 tasks from 117 sources, eleven models and ten retained single-turn responses per task/effort. No tools, new experiments or iterative feedback; rationale grading uses a separate Astra.
research.counterexample: High molecular-structure credit coexists with roughly half-credit selection/prediction. Historical-case agreement is not a newly discovered or experimentally effective medicine.
research.evidence: Read paper construction, grading, results, discussion and methods. Paper dated November 9, announcement November 20. Preserve partial-credit averaging, completed invalid outputs zero and recovery of incomplete calls.
research.limits: Reference-dependent grading, possible training exposure, no independently established human grader validation, and earlier image-encoding issue. The announcement’s GPT-6.2 score is not part of the paper’s cohort.
research.mitigation: Validate research choices and results independently, including experiments and full-process costs; separate interpretation from prospective success.
research.readerContext: Read R1 and related news examples in Japanese/English, research-cycle graph and R1-R2. Explain retrospective evidence in place; do not infer biological misuse from therapeutic task scores.
research.whyHere: Add MedChemBench and METR task-creation evidence to R1 without downgrading existing observed assistance or claiming whole-development gains. R1-R2 already requires useful bottleneck relief.

cycle.mechanism: A fitted capability-growth slope does not by itself identify an AI-driven improvement loop or its causal contribution to development speed.
cycle.conditions: MCI uses tested public models through Astra and Opus 5.5. Developer-specific calibration and breakpoints differ from the combined frontier; private-data assessments are separate.
cycle.counterexample: No clear combined-frontier acceleration can coexist with AI accelerating development relative to an unobserved slower AI-free counterfactual.
cycle.evidence: Read 3.C.2, discussion and Appendix H. Positive developer-specific slope changes depend on calibration, breakpoint and benchmark; intervals are wide.
cycle.limits: Public release lags, absent private models and absent AI-free counterfactual. This is not a direct replication or refutation of the October private Anthropic assessment, nor proof of absent RSI.
cycle.mitigation: Track useful successive improvements, whole-process costs and independent validation across generations rather than interpreting one fitted trend as causal attribution.
cycle.readerContext: Read R3 in both languages and development-paths/research-cycle context. Distinguish human-assisted RSI from fully autonomous successor development and sustained acceleration.
cycle.whyHere: Preserve the existing bounded two-round experiment and limited/tested classification. R2-R3 and R3-R2 still require repeated useful gains and remaining constraints.

primary.support: Public-frontier trend uncertainty, developer calibration and unavailable counterfactual.

safety.mechanism: Automated attacks can help improve defenses, but creating and evaluating safeguards still requires independent judgment, human investigation and operational controls.
safety.conditions: OpenAI compares adaptive black-box extraction tests over six attacker models, with old Astra and new 6.2 Astra safeguard stacks. Existing Anvil tests have privileged access; fuzzy experiments use a controlled Terra checkpoint.
safety.counterexample: A lower reasoning-extraction rate does not prove an equally lower harmful-capability transfer rate, resolved alignment or prevention of global harm. Stronger adaptive attacks remain a counterexample to blanket safety.
safety.evidence: Read the full November 20 defense account and substantively reread R4’s bounded alignment-research, Anvil, fuzzy robustness and stopped-evaluation evidence. R4 was due November 21.
safety.limits: Extraction table omits counts, budgets and false blocks; model/stack changes are confounded. Fuzzy safety has a benign-cyber cost; a stopped real evaluation was detected without confirmed completed recovery.
safety.mitigation: Combine independent evaluation, human oversight, access controls and recovery; report budgets and benign-task costs. Separate researcher and evaluator roles and test durability after further training.
safety.readerContext: Read R4/M3 in Japanese/English, their full existing body and new paragraphs, related tours, misuse summary, R4 safeguard and news guidance. Preserve historical dates and original scopes of unchanged summaries.
safety.whyHere: Retain R4 limited/tested and M3 hypothesis. Renew seven substantively updated node clocks and five matching evidence clocks only. R4-C1, R0-R4 and M3-H keep conditional wording and dates.
